paper: Gifford, Jastrzębowska, Singer and Cichy 2025, Nature Human Behaviour
title: Driving two visual regions together or apart

steps.title: Model the brain first
steps.paper: The authors trained an fMRI encoding model for each participant on the Natural Scenes Dataset, covering early and higher visual areas. They then tested the models on a separate out-of-distribution image set.
steps.here: This app trains nothing. TRIBE, a ready-made brain model, predicts responses to scenes that Isaac renders, and early visual cortex stands in for V1 as an anatomical region.

steps.title: Predict responses to every image
steps.paper: The models generated in silico responses for every image in the dataset, for each participant. Each area's response was averaged across its voxels.
steps.here: The study scored every rendered item in both regions. The lateral occipital region stands in for V4.

steps.title: Find images that align
steps.paper: For each pair of areas, a search over all the images looked for ones that aligned the two responses, driving both areas or suppressing both.
steps.here: The same search runs over the rendered items. These are the items that drive both regions up together.

steps.title: Find images that disentangle
steps.paper: The search also looked for images that disentangled the two areas, driving one while suppressing the other. The chosen images were compared against baseline images that were not optimized.
steps.here: These are the items that raise early visual cortex more than the lateral occipital region. The opposite set sits beside them in the same findings view.

steps.title: Recheck under new conditions
steps.paper: The controlling images were checked across participants, so results held beyond the participant they were found for.
steps.here: The app has no other participants, so it pairs the items chosen each way and reruns them from a camera angle the search never saw. This is a held-out view, not a held-out brain.

args.title: Chosen items from a new camera angle

bindings.a: an item chosen for early visual cortex over the lateral occipital region
bindings.b: an item chosen for the lateral occipital region over early visual cortex

steps.title: Change the images, compare again
steps.paper: The authors repeated the analyses with other image sets, and with encoding models trained on other data.
steps.here: The app cannot swap image sets, so it previews the same items in greyscale. That changes how the items look, not which items there are.

steps.title: Test in real brains
steps.paper: New participants viewed the V1-versus-V4 controlling images in the scanner, with both areas mapped for each person. Their measured responses were compared with what the models predicted.
steps.here: The app cannot scan anyone. It lists the chosen items and their sources so a lab can show them to real people.
